title: The two-dimensional pressure structure of the HD 163296 protoplanetary disk as probed by multi-molecule kinematics
question: Whether the vertical (2D) thermal stratification of the HD 163296 disk is detectable in the rotation curves of seven molecular tracers, and what disk mass, scale radius and 2D pressure structure follow from a multi-molecule stratified fit

data.angular_resolution: 0.15'' for 12CO, 13CO, C18O, HCN, C2H (per Table 1); 0.3'' for H2CO and HCO+ (the two lower-resolution lines)

what.value: 2D gas kinetic temperature structure T(R,z) (Dullemond et al. 2020 parameterization, seven fitted parameters in Table 1: T_atm,0=63 K, q_atm=-0.61, T_mid,0=24 K, q_mid=-0.18, alpha=3.01, z0=9 au, beta=0.42)

evidence.quote: we use the kinetic temperature by (cite: maps4) and the observed brightness temperature from the data

what.value: Parametric emitting-layer fits z(R) for each molecule (Z0, phi, r_taper, psi in Table 2), plus nonparametric emitting layers

evidence.quote: Best-fit parameters for the molecular emitting layers for HD 163296 fitted by (cite: paneque).
adopting nonparametric emitting layers for all the molecules, as retrieved by (cite: paneque)

what.value: Disk geometry: i=46.7 deg, PA=313.3 deg
Hyperfine frequency shifts: 2.5 MHz (C2H), 2.09 MHz and 1.54 MHz (HCN)

external_data.citation: (cite: sastry1981; muller2000) and (cite: ahrens2002), via CDMS

what.value: Isothermal comparison model: H/R=0.084 and q=-0.84
Two-molecule stratified fit results (M_star, M_d, R_c) used for comparison in Table 3

evidence.quote: We also compare our results with the ones obtained by (cite: martire)

recipe.goal: Select molecular lines from the MAPS cubes
recipe.method: Visual cube exploration; lines chosen by brightness and high S/N

recipe.goal: Derive molecular optical depth profiles to check emitting layers
recipe.method: Radial surface brightness from the data compared with the optically thick Planck brightness at the assumed emitting layer; tau = -ln(1 - I_data/I_Planck)
key_parameters: 30 deg wedge along the disk major axis for the radial profile
assumptions: Kinetic temperature at the emitting layer from the Dullemond et al. (2020) T(R,z) with MAPS parameters; LTE, optically thick reference emission

recipe.goal: Extract rotation curves with eddy (SHO method)
recipe.method: Fit each spectrum with a Gaussian to get its centroid, then fit centroids in each annulus with a cosine (harmonic) function to get v_theta
key_parameters: i=46.7 deg, PA=313.3 deg, zero center offsets
Extraction repeated 20 times with independent spectrum samples; uncertainty = weighted standard deviation
assumptions: Exponentially tapered power-law emitting layers z(R) with Paneque et al. parameters; azimuthal symmetry; front side dominates

recipe.goal: Rotation curves of hyperfine lines (C2H, HCN)
recipe.method: New multi-Gaussian (double for C2H, triple for HCN) spectrum fit in eddy with shared width and fixed hyperfine velocity shifts
key_parameters: Equal Gaussian width for all components
Fixed shifts: 2.5 MHz (C2H), 2.09 and 1.54 MHz (HCN); sigma bounded to half the component separation; intensity ratio priors xi in [0.2,1.5] (C2H) and [0.1,1] (HCN)

recipe.goal: Test beam smearing in rotation curves
recipe.method: Correlate radial intensity gradient of the line with the velocity difference between C2H (or HCN) and 12CO rotation curves
assumptions: 12CO curve used as smooth Keplerian reference

recipe.goal: Simultaneous multi-molecule fit of the seven curves with the stratified model
recipe.method: MCMC maximisation of the likelihood of one stratified rotation-curve model fitted to all seven curves for M_star, M_d, R_c
assumptions: gamma = 1 in the surface density; temperature structure fixed from MAPS (uncertainties not propagated); emitting layers from Paneque et al.

recipe.method: Combine fitted disk mass and scale radius with the assumed T(R,z) to compute P(R,z)
assumptions: Barotropic fluid; shape of P(R,z) set by the assumed temperature structure

recipe.goal: Compare stratified and isothermal predictions of velocity differences vs C18O
recipe.method: Normalised difference of squared rotation velocities of each molecule relative to C18O, compared with isothermal and stratified model predictions
key_parameters: Isothermal model with H/R=0.084 and q=-0.84

recipe.goal: Test dependence on the assumed emitting layers
recipe.method: Repeat extraction and multi-molecule fit with (a) flat midplane emission for all molecules and (b) nonparametric emitting layers

evidence.quote: the estimate of the stellar mass does not change between the isothermal and stratified fits

answer_key.quantity: Nonparametric vs parametric layers: M_d difference
Peak optical depths of the two optically thin lines (molecule names missing in text)

evidence.quote: reaching maximum peaks at $\tau \sim 0.11$ and $\tau \sim 0.45$ respectively
a local maximum around the radius of the intensity peak ($R=109$ au)

score_reason: Public data and public fitting code with a tabulated numeric result, but the MAPS products, eddy settings, radial ranges and fit priors are not given, and the modified eddy is not stated as released.
rediscovery_reason: MAPS data are public, DySc is public, the model and emcee setup are described, and the main results are numeric (M_star, M_d, R_c), though eddy settings must be inferred.
